literature_notes: Both ledger lines (L1, L2) describe the identical construct: full-length LRRTM4 with CFP fused to the C-terminus (LRRTM4-CFP), published in PMC2746109. LRRTM4 is a type I single-pass transmembrane protein with signal peptide 1–30 (cleaved), extracellular domain 31–424, TM helix 425–445, and intracellular C-tail 446–590. A C-terminal CFP fusion therefore places the tag after residue 590, which is deep in the intracellular domain — not on the extracellular face. The construct is not a snorkel design. The robust synaptogenic activity (L2) confirms the protein traffics correctly to the neuronal surface and is functional, but this validates the full-length protein, not an extracellular tag position. No ledger line reports any insertion in the extracellular domain (31–424), at the mature N-terminus (after residue 30), or in any extracellular loop. Zero extracellular surface tag sites are supported by this ledger.

literature_other_positions.note: CFP fused after the last residue (N590) of LRRTM4; the C-terminus lies in the intracellular domain (residues 446–590), so this tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular space.
